... One more things in consideration

# About a globally distributed database
... partitioned by nature of
a) the peer-to-peer way (data accessed and modified locally by users on users' devices),
b) the centrally managed indexes, tokenizing parser scripts, and data schema recipes for structuring data and validation

## Quick summary of the forementioned, as readily presented on this timeline (Fb/santappl):

- users see content in real-time and some have an extension installed, which looks for hashtags
... upon discovery, at the minimum, a checksum is calculated, based on a data schema that is located on jstr.co (in this example... for other examples refer to Maduk - Vermilion in Temple Ruin post edits, Fluid ft Veela - Subsurface & Blackmill ft Veela - Let It Be -- and more that tokenize unstructured data in an onion-like way, elsewhere)

- besides (eg.) Facebook's servers, storing and parsing data, a second entry is stored in jstr.co, centrally, temporary for some users who cache hot posts in-browser, and permanently with users who use Node.js with a checksum/blockchain component

## What about deep insight into contents -- privacy concerns upon aggregation
... aggregating of data and statistically derived counterparts is a consequence of running documented methods, on observable metrics, with repeatable results

- besides the key data nodes, storing contents that provide overview further back -- that is the #LeapGesture posts which are data points that, for some values, provide quantification on habits to map on a graph, wrapped and contextualised with content (on timeline)

- encrypted content is distributed in an especially limited manner -- to a circle of people that any given person may choose themselves -- and it may only be decrypted when a "composite key" (in sense of a password, assembled)

- as optimization is not the issue, the more important privacy in combination with the need for automation (enabling access despite of an explicit grant) implies that a password should either be a general function of combination or  of some words, or a custom (JavaScript) function that some people may provide by grant
... eg. values and keywords/phrases (and perhaps, synonyms, etc), likely known or readily available to a big enough group of close peers

## Further notes on storage mediums and partitioning, thus invoked

- Scalable Vector Graphics files are especially suitable for storing modifications and overlapping/interlacing of words, as well as data that is either best contained or presented in form of style and animated transitions
... combination with music and dictionaries is not excluded

- because schema may not be uniform on one platform for all users (eg. Facebook), there might be a need for database migrations that are invoked upon visiting related resources (eg. music videos)
... .js on-ion files may contain JSON schema definitions with remapping patterns that transform data structure with a definitive outcome (resulting in a changes in schema for all database entries), or variable changes (just for some users)

- for the current, central version of database structures (schema, methods and public data), jstr.org key-pair store with Trie Index access
... first come first serve basis on determining the optimal trie route crossroads, with platform enabled differentiation of content data nodes in schema (eg. the "fbclid" token on Facebook links, user ids), not excluding the more costly content patterns (such as partially matching contents -- see Google's "diff-match-patch" JavaScript library)

- parsing contents in unstructured documents to a tree structure of tokens is provided either by scripts from Node Package Manager (npmjs.com) that use a given library (eg. a Markdown parsing package), or using .jsonion files with a text2json parsing library, or even using a service application endpoint on a prescribed URL
... validation is possible by wrapping libraries' outcomes in a hashing/checksum function with a validation schema -- granular validation of subsections or partial may be available, if so defined ahead in the script

- validation outcomes may be reviewed, by looking at an abbreviated schema and evaluated outcomes (successful and deviant results, as compared with peers)
